scope: Static source and artifact review of the proposed 384 MiB / 15 s scanner-probe boundary and the pinned 1,356-input comparator workload. No detector measurement, fixture execution, candidate import, build, or probe was performed.
axes: hard resource isolation and process-tree cleanup
bounded comparator output and result provenance
fixed-population input integrity without recursive self-copy
summary: The cap is not by itself a safe bound for the existing 1,356-input comparator. Its 384 MiB limit is per worker process; its 15 s SIGALRM is set after candidate-module import and reset for each file, while each of two sequential worker invocations has a 600 s direct-child timeout. Candidate-controlled stdout is captured without a byte limit and doubles as the result protocol. One child per seat also does not cap concurrent children across a wave. The current pinned corpus freezer does avoid recursive self-copy by enumerating a pinned Git commit and writing to a fresh staging directory; preserve that invariant.

findings.title: The 15-second comparator alarm is not a hard whole-run deadline
findings.exploit_path: [INFERENCE, not executed] The comparator imports the selected scanner before installing SIGALRM. Import-time code can therefore run outside the 15-second alarm; imported code can also replace/cancel the process-local handler before or during a scan. The alarm is restarted for each manifest row, so it is not a 15-second bound for a 1,356-row pass. The parent only supplies a 600-second timeout for each of the two sequential worker subprocesses, and no process-group cleanup is present in that launch path.

evidence.observation: RLIMIT_AS is set, then the candidate module is imported at lines 41-43; SIGALRM is installed only at line 44 and alarm(15) is set/reset around each scan_file call.
Before/after workers run sequentially via subprocess.run(timeout=600); the comparator does not start a new session or kill a process group.
The prior static review independently records that candidate code can replace/cancel the in-process SIGALRM; it did not run a timeout-bypass probe.

findings.impact: An import or scan can consume substantially more than the advertised 15 seconds; descendants launched by candidate code are not shown to be killed with the direct worker. A timeout/error cannot be treated as proof that the process tree has stopped.
findings.smallest_remediation: Do not run a candidate in this proposal-only phase. For a later authorized run, enforce the wall deadline from a trusted parent and place the complete worker tree in a killable process group/cgroup; kill and reap the group on timeout rather than trusting candidate-process signal handlers.

findings.title: Candidate stdout is both the result channel and an unbounded parent allocation
findings.exploit_path: [INFERENCE, not executed] The worker imports candidate code and emits its own JSON rows to stdout. The parent uses capture_output=True and parses the entire stdout into rows, then retains both complete runs. Candidate module code can write arbitrary bytes/JSON to the same pipe during import or scanning, forging the expected row stream or causing parent memory growth beyond the child's address-space limit.

evidence.observation: Candidate module import and worker protocol emission share stdout.
The parent captures all stdout, parses all lines, and retains both run arrays before producing the comparison. No output-byte or row-size limit is applied.
Prior source-only review documents the same worker-stdout forgery path and post-run hash attribution weakness; no attack was executed.

findings.impact: The comparison can be forged without completing scans, and untrusted output can exhaust parent memory despite the 384 MiB worker limit. A well-formed row count does not prove scan completion or provenance.
findings.smallest_remediation: Separate candidate stdout from a trusted parent-owned result channel; stream and validate one manifest row at a time with strict per-row and total-output byte caps. Treat truncation, malformed output, or an uncompleted worker as an explicit error.

findings.title: One-child-per-seat is not a wave-wide concurrency limit
findings.exploit_path: [INFERENCE, conditional] If each concurrently dispatched seat uses its one-child allowance, the per-seat rule permits 64 concurrent top-level children in this recorded wave and up to 100 at the configured wave maximum. Each child may address up to 384 MiB; this is up to 24 GiB or 37.5 GiB of aggregate per-process virtual-address-space allowance respectively, not a prediction of resident-memory use. Descendants are not counted by the per-seat rule.

evidence.observation: The proposed bound is one child at a time per seat, 384 MiB address space, 15 s. It does not define a global semaphore or total process-tree budget.
The dispatch record reports 64 spawned seats and a 100-lane wave maximum. This is dispatch capacity evidence, not evidence that 64 scanner children ran.
A single comparator invocation runs its before/after workers sequentially, but that does not serialize separate seat invocations.

findings.impact: Simultaneous scans can multiply CPU, I/O, process count, and memory pressure. The stated per-seat cap does not establish safe aggregate host resource usage.
findings.smallest_remediation: Keep this wave source-only as specified. For a later authorized full-corpus comparison, admit at most one resource-heavy comparator globally at a time; if candidate code is in scope as untrusted, enforce aggregate memory and PID limits on its entire process tree in addition to the per-process RLIMIT_AS.

findings.title: The pinned corpus freezer currently avoids recursive self-copy
findings.exploit_path: No self-copy exploit is identified in the existing frozen-corpus construction path. The freezer selects only regular .jsonl blobs from a pinned Git commit, rejects absolute, empty, dot, and parent path components, reads bytes from that commit, stages a new snapshot, refuses to overwrite an existing snapshot, and publishes by rename. The comparator iterates the pinned manifest instead of recursively walking its output directory.

evidence.observation: The base commit is fixed; enumeration is from Git tree blobs with regular-file mode and traversal checks.
Existing snapshot output is refused; bytes are staged from git show and published by rename.
The pinned manifest declares 1,356 inputs. The prior corpus review reports 1,356 distinct path strings.

findings.impact: The present recipe does not recursively absorb its own generated snapshot. Replacing it with a recursive working-tree copy/walk, or placing generated output under an enumerated source root, would reintroduce self-ingestion and workload growth.
findings.smallest_remediation: Preserve the pinned-commit manifest and fresh-stage approach; do not enumerate or copy the current output tree into itself. Keep snapshot generation separate from any future comparison output.

evidence.observation: Helper following has a same-function recursion guard, depth limit 4, and per-cell descent budget 2,000; shell classification also has an explicit depth guard at lines 1084-1087.

scanner_recursion_note.limit: These source-level traversal guards do not sandbox candidate-module import, bound stdout, prevent operating-system child creation, or replace an external process-tree deadline.

unknowns: No round-22 candidate scanner bytes or proposed round-22 comparator implementation were measured or executed.
No detector probe, fixture payload, build, test, lint, or smoke run was performed.
The actual number of scanner children launched by any wave seat is unobserved; the lane counts above describe dispatch capacity only.
No process-tree memory/PID accounting was performed, and no aggregate resident-memory result is claimed.
